extracted.intended_audience: general scientifically-interested public / subscribers to Popular Science Monthly
extracted.subtask_description: Short popular-science magazine pieces that summarize observations, experiments, inventions, and natural-history notes for a general audience; emphasizes clear reporting of methods, notable results, practical implications, and illustrative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wild-silk suitability (reeleability vs spinnability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cocoons can not be reeled, but the fiber is exceedingly well adapted for spinning, can be dyed and printed easily and satisfactorily, and forms a cloth of 'incredible durability, the life of one person being seldom sufficient to wear out a garment made of it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species differ: Attacus ricini (cannot be reeled but spins well), Attacus cynthia (domesticated; not adapted for reeling but spins well), Anthercea Assama (Muga silk; bleaches and dyes well), Anthercea paphia (Tusser silk; widely distributed). Practical uses: wall-hangings, curtains, coverlets, furniture-work; not suited where extreme fineness is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silk fiber cross-section and appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: The fiber of this silk is flat, thereby showing a strong difference from that of the mulberry silk, which is round, and to this is ascribed its glassy look.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flat fiber yields a different luster and 'richer and softer surface' after weaving; this property can be an advantage rather than a drawback when the fiber is suitably processed in the loom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silk dyeability and processing obstacles
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief obstacle to the general introduction of this silk is the difficulty with which it is made to take colors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed solutions: applying oxygen to the natural coloring matter (effective but too expensive for general use); more thorough cleansing of the native product and better reeling (partial solution) — these allow the silk to submit to dyeing and printing 'in a tolerably satisfactory manner.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for successful Sahara fertilization/irrigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Fertility is exhibited wherever water has been brought to the surface of the soil. Henceforth it will be safe to say that the transformation of the Sahara is only a question of time, labor, artesian wells, means of communication, and security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful transformation requires access to subterranean water, modest effort to bring it to the surface, supportive infrastructure (communication), labor investment, and secure conditions; evidence includes medals awarded for plants raised on irrigated Saharan soil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraction and identification of characine (source of marsh-odors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characine is obtained by first drying the algae in the air, and then covering them again with cold water; after eight or ten hours a thin iridescent layer appears on the surface — this is the odorous substance; ether dissolves the characine and leaves it as a white, greasy, volatile substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: lighter than water, forms minute pellicles, very sparingly soluble, soluble in alcohol and ether, hardly soluble in water, strong marsh odor, volatile and subject to oxidation. Methodological note: decanting, ether extraction, and evaporation yield the substance for study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for fossil ferment identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Microscopic examination of silicified radicles of conifers in phytogenic rocks shows precisely the same characteristic marks of alteration as are seen in corresponding radicles of the present epoch which have become the prey of the bacillus (butyric ferment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: morphological correspondence between fossil and modern altered tissues; legitimate inference that identical reactions (butyric fermentation) occurred in the geological past when the same characteristic alterations are observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for electric horse-subduing apparatus
rubrics_metrics.description: By turning a handle attached to the electro-magnet, a current is formed which affects the horse's mouth, and so surprises him that he stops and stands still. The current is not strong enough to stupefy the animal; it rather produces in him astonishment, and a disagreeable but not painful sensation of an electrical pricking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desirable properties: simple machinery; placed within easy reach of the driver/rider; safe (non-injurious, not stupefying); effective on otherwise dangerous horses; combined with soothing manner and caresses for best results. Empirical support: multiple reported trials (Omnibus Company, Cab Company) with dangerous horses rendered manageable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use guidelines for electrical stick/switch
rubrics_metrics.description: It is enough to jog him with the legs as he is preparing to rise, and at the same time apply the points of the electric stick to the top of his shoulders. He will immediately subside and let his head down... when a horse tries to turn around, the application of the current to that side of his face toward which he is about to turn will cause him to stop immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique: timed, targeted application (shoulders to stop rearing; side of face to stop turning); instrument description: riding-whip containing two insulated conducting wires connected to a magneto-electric apparatus. Emphasize control and restraint without pain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation-based criterion for 'automatism' in portrait-sketching
rubrics_metrics.description: A designer making an extemporaneous sketch of a head involuntarily reproduces his own portrait... a person tracing with a pencil figures of spontaneous conception will always produce the same head unless he is copying from or imitating a model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for evaluating quick sketches: look for consistent, repeatable personal/ethnographic traits; comparisons across pupils show each tends to 'reproduce himself' more or less; sex and personal preferences influence recurring types. Use as an interpretive lens rather than a prescriptive rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Architectural echo-suppression technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Cords stretched in a kind of network near the ceiling have been recommended for destroying echoes in churches and public halls... When metallic wires are used in the same manner, the resonance is greatly diminished, and is sometimes converted into a musical sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical evidence: successfully tried in St. Peter's Church (Geneva) and the Assembly Hall of Bordeaux. Note possible side-effect: metallic wires can convert resonance into musical tones; phenomenon explanation: rapid reflections between opposite surfaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic criteria for 'stammering of the vocal cords'
rubrics_metrics.description: The disease appears to be due to defective coordination of certain muscles of the larynx, in consequence of which the vocal apparatus fails at intervals to fully obey the will; the movements required for articulating syllables are perfectly performed, but the production of vocal sound is at intervals suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differential diagnosis: articulate ability preserved while vocal sound production is intermittently arrested; isolated sounds usually correctly articulated; rapid emission of certain combinations prone to sudden arrest. Diagnosis aided by direct ocular observation with specialized appliances; distinct diagnosis allows effective treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and reporting standards for stature statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly three hundred observations of the height and span of the Japanese: average height five feet three inches, span four feet eleven inches; in twenty-four women taken at random the average was four feet eight inches with an average span of four feet six inches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size, present averages and distributions (percent of sample with span less than height, greater, or equal), note outliers (tallest measurement), and discuss possible causal factors (climate, heating methods, diet, hereditary influences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria for hearing-aid instruments (audiphone, dentaphone, osteophone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The audiphone and dentaphone have been objected to: the audiphone to a certain extent obscures the features of the person using it — the dentaphone is held more or less in the line of vision; and both instruments require the constant service of the hands when in use. The osteophone consists of a large receiving diaphragm attached to a rod to be held between the teeth, leaving the hands free and being comparatively inconspicuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design desiderata: hands-free operation, inconspicuous appearance, effective sound transmission. Clinical suitability: audiphone/dentaphone/instruments are mainly useful in acoustic deafness (middle-ear disease cases often better served by ear-trumpet); empirical caution that many expectations have been disappointed and suitable cases are few and far between. Materials and constructions suggested: Fuller's cardboard with shellac, yellow pine trumpet shape, rods conveying vibrations between skulls, ornamental fan prototypes for occasional use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting leather-bookbinding deterioration and gaslight exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses show morocco little affected, common sheep attacked, Russia leather and calf badly acted upon; an acid taste and acid reaction increase with decay; sulphuric acid and ammonia were found in extracts; conclusion: bindings of Russia, calf, or sheep absorb sulphuric acid when exposed to the products of the combustion of illuminating gas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method: compare fresh leather extracts vs decayed samples; quantify percent sulphuric acid and ammonia; consider alternative hypotheses (disintegration preceding acid absorption). Practical implication: gaslight combustion products likely contribute to leather decay; recommend further experiments to determine sequence of disintegration and absorption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for producing low-cost household light via phosphorescence
rubrics_metrics.description: With a comparatively feeble electric current, Dr. Phipson perceptibly increased the phosphorescence of certain bodies (e.g., sulphuret of barium) enclosed in a Geissler tube; by causing a constant current of a certain intensity to pass through the tube, he obtains a uniform and agreeable light at an expense he estimates to be less than that of gaslight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparatus: Geissler tube containing a rarefied gas and a phosphorescent body; apply a constant current of specified intensity. Note this is an experimental proposal with claimed cost advantage — report intensity, stability, and user acceptability when assessing viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptive morphology criterion for deep-sea organisms
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire absence of sunlight on the deep-sea bottom seems to have the same effect as the darkness of caves, in reducing to a rudimentary condition the eyes of fish and Crustacea which ordinarily enjoy visual power; many of these are provided with enormously long and delicate feelers or hairs, with which they feel their way about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating deep-sea morphology, expect regression of visual organs and compensatory enhancement of tactile/chemosensory structures; interpret long feelers/hairs as adaptive sensory compensation for darkness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of tobacco adulteration (camomile-flower substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preparation sold under the name of 'The New Smoking Mixture' was found on examination to be about one third tobacco and two thirds camomile-flowers; camomile-flowers are first deprived of their bitter principle by exhaustion in water, then colored, sweetened, and dried for mixing with cut tobacco.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical approach: chemical/organoleptic analysis to detect non-tobacco plant matter and processing markers (loss of bitter principle, added colorants/sweeteners); practical outcome: detect and stop fraudulent adulteration in commercial products.
